problem: Whether variance alone forces a lower bound on the normalized Turán deficit δk of Poisson-binomial laws, specifically whether δk ≥ κ/V holds near the mode for a universal constant κ > 0.
debate: Log-concavity and Turán-type inequalities for Bernoulli sums, including bounds from ultra-log-concavity, Newton's inequalities, and modal-index theory.
gap: Known lower bounds on δk depend on n, on individual success probabilities, or on k alone, and all degenerate when near-zero and near-one probabilities accumulate at fixed variance; none are variance-scaled without other dependence.
contribution: Proof that V·δ_D ≥ 1/4 with tight bounds showing the optimal constant κ⋆ lies between 1/4 and 1/3, plus explicit bounds at every index via Hillion-Johnson cubic inequalities, proved using Bernstein expansions.
note: Technically strong result addressing a natural question with non-trivial bounds and an explicit lower family; ready for peer review.
